idea.title: Transit Copilot
idea.text: A phone app that watches the city's live bus/tram feeds and proactively reroutes commuters BEFORE a delay is officially announced, by detecting anomalies in vehicle telemetry. Tech: public GTFS-RT feeds + a small anomaly model. Wow moment: the app buzzes 'leave 4 min early, take line 3' while the official app still shows everything on time.

intake.restatement: An app that predicts public-transport delays from live telemetry anomalies and reroutes users before official announcements.
implicit_assumptions: the city's real-time feed is granular enough to detect anomalies early
users will trust a prediction that contradicts the official app
a useful anomaly model can be trained or tuned within 24h
intake.open_question: How many minutes of advance warning does the telemetry actually give over the official alerts?

judge.verdict: GTFS-RT feeds are public and well-documented, so the data path is real; the risk is the anomaly model eating the night. The two grids agree here: strong demo potential AND feasible.
strengths: demo tells itself: two phones side by side
watchouts: model tuning is a time sink
proposed_tests: replay yesterday's feed tonight and count detectable anomalies
judge.viable_scope: One single bus line, threshold-based anomaly detection (no ML), two-phone comparison demo.

believer.verdict: Citymapper won by being 10 minutes smarter than official apps; being EARLIER than official alerts is the same wedge, sharper. The upside is a transit authority pilot.
strengths: measurable head start over official info
watchouts: differentiation depends on the feed's latency edge
proposed_tests: measure the real gap between telemetry anomaly and official alert on 10 incidents

precedents.name: Citymapper
precedents.why_comparable: won commuters by beating official transit info quality

scientist_eval.verdict: Anomaly detection on GTFS-RT streams is a real, published line of work; nothing here contradicts the literature. The idea slightly oversells 'prediction' — the papers detect, they rarely forecast.
strengths: published precedent for transit anomaly detection
watchouts: forecast horizon claims beyond the literature
proposed_tests: reproduce a published detection baseline on the local feed

references.title: Real-time anomaly detection in public transit feeds (retrieved via Semantic Scholar)

skeptic.verdict: The whole value rests on an unmeasured number: the lead time over official alerts. If it is 90 seconds, the app is a gimmick. Live-feed demos also love to die on stage.
strengths: the pitch is understood in one sentence
watchouts: lead time over official alerts is unmeasured
live feed may be quiet during the 3-minute demo
commuters may not act on unofficial warnings
proposed_tests: log 24h of feed vs official alerts and compute the median lead time
record a backup replay of a real incident for the demo
ask 5 commuters if they would leave earlier on an unofficial warning

investor.verdict: Cities are actively buying rider-experience tech and the feeds just became mandatory in the EU — the timing is the strongest part. Monetization is B2G, slow but real.
strengths: regulatory tailwind on open transit data
watchouts: B2G sales cycles outlive hackathon momentum
proposed_tests: find one transit authority innovation contact and ask for 15 minutes

strategist.verdict: Commuter-first is the right first angle for a demo; the copyable part is the UI, the defensible part is the anomaly lead-time know-how. Build the measurement first, the app second.
strengths: sequencing: measure lead time before building UI
watchouts: a weekend team could copy the UI shell
proposed_tests: publish the measured lead-time stat in the pitch
strategist.alternative_angle: Sell the anomaly stream to the transit authority as an ops-alerting API instead of a consumer app — fewer users needed, faster to credibility.

jury.verdict: 'We warn you before the city does' — I can repeat that at deliberation. I will believe the demo only if I see both phones live; a canned video loses half the points.
proposed_tests: rehearse the two-phone moment five times
jury.retained_sentence: They warn you before the city does.

judge.verdict: Maintained: the skeptic's lead-time doubt is real but it is measurable tonight, which makes it a task, not a blocker.
proposed_tests: run the 24h feed log before writing app code
judge.viable_scope: One line, threshold detection, replay-backed demo.

believer.verdict: Revised down one point: the skeptic is right that the wedge is an unmeasured number. If the median lead time beats 5 minutes, my 8 stands.
strengths: sharp wedge if the number holds
believer.revision: lowered 8 to 7 pending the lead-time measurement

precedents.name: Citymapper
precedents.why_comparable: beat official transit info as its wedge

scientist_eval.verdict: Maintained. Keep the claim at 'detects anomalies earlier', not 'predicts delays' — that phrasing stays inside what the retrieved literature supports.
strengths: grounded claim available for the pitch

references.title: Real-time anomaly detection in public transit feeds (retrieved via Semantic Scholar)

skeptic.verdict: Raised one point: the judge's replay-backed demo plan neutralizes my stage-death objection. The lead-time question stands and stays the first task.
strengths: team has a measurable go/no-go test
skeptic.revision: raised 5 to 6: replay backup addresses demo fragility

investor.verdict: Maintained; the strategist's ops-API alternative is the version I would actually take a second meeting on.

strategist.verdict: Maintained: demo as consumer app for the wow, pitch the ops API as the business — both angles in one storyline.
proposed_tests: pitch rehearsal with the dual angle
strategist.alternative_angle: Ops-alerting API for the transit authority.

jury.verdict: Maintained, credibility up one: a live attempt with a replay fallback is exactly what a tired jury respects.
jury.revision: raised demo_credibility after the replay-backup plan
jury.retained_sentence: They warn you before the city does.

synthesis.consensus: Feasible in 24h on public data with a demo that explains itself; every agent conditions the upside on one unmeasured number — the lead time over official alerts.

disagreements.positions: believer: the wedge is Citymapper-grade if it holds; skeptic: it may be 90 seconds of nothing
disagreements.why_it_matters: the entire differentiation is this number

synthesis.action: Tonight, before any app code: log 24h of feed vs official alerts and compute the median lead time.
